exercises.title: Differentiate a Two-Layer Network
exercises.focus: Nonlinearity; chain rule; every weight and bias gradient
exercises.why: A learned linear map cannot express nonlinear decision boundaries. Building one small nonlinear network connects scalar differentiation to neural-network training.
exercises.brief: Implement forward_and_grad(params,x,target) for one example, returning (prediction,loss,grads). params has W1 (H rows, D columns), b1 (H numbers), W2 (H numbers), b2 (one number). x has D numbers. Compute hidden[j]=tanh(sum(W1[j][k]*x[k])+b1[j]), prediction=sum(W2[j]*hidden[j])+b2, and loss=0.5*(prediction-target)^2. grads has the same keys and nested shapes as params, containing every analytic partial derivative of loss. Do not update or mutate inputs. Assume matching nonempty dimensions and finite real inputs. Start with one input and one hidden unit; draw every dependency. Use the chain rule and tanh derivative, not finite differences, inside your implementation. Numerical differences belong in independent tests. Then write one gradient-descent step using these gradients and show loss decreases at a small step size. This is a scalar-output MLP, not a transformer yet.

# Differentiate a Two-Layer Network

## Predict
Work through the smallest example by hand before coding.

## Derive
Explain the equations and dimensions in words; no tensor library assumptions.

## Evidence
Record a failure, root cause, and independent candidate test.

## Transfer
What changes in batched tensor code? What is invariant? Explain what these tests cannot establish about a trained transformer.

hints: Write the scalar prediction and loss before any gradients. W1 has one row per hidden unit; W2 combines those units.
Differentiate loss with respect to prediction, then each hidden output, then its pre-activation. tanh derivative is 1-hidden^2.
A bias has local derivative 1; a weight has local derivative equal to its input. Check each coordinate independently, including both biases.

exercises.title: Build Causal Self-Attention
exercises.focus: Dot products; scale; stable normalization; information boundaries
exercises.why: Attention lets each position combine previous token information. The causal mask is a correctness boundary: future text must not affect earlier outputs.
exercises.brief: Implement causal_attention(queries,keys,values), returning (outputs,weights). There are T positions; query/key rows each contain D numbers; value rows each contain V numbers. All dimensions match, D and V are positive, and inputs are finite. If T=0 return ([],[]). At position i, score[j]=dot(queries[i],keys[j])/sqrt(D) for j<=i. Softmax only these allowed scores, with max subtraction for stability. weights is a T-by-T list with EXACT zeros at j>i. outputs[i] is the weighted sum of value rows. Do not mutate inputs. No learned projection matrices or multiple heads yet: queries and keys determine relevance, values are the content mixed. Derive the all-zero-score case by hand. Prove with a test that changing every future key/value cannot affect an earlier output; test scaling with D>1 and extreme scores. This primitive becomes one attention head inside a decoder block.

hints: At the first position, only one value is allowed, so its attention weight must be exactly one.
Mask before normalization. Including future scores in the softmax denominator still leaks future information even if you later zero their weights.

exercises.title: Align Next-Token Targets and Loss Masks
exercises.focus: Teacher forcing; next-token alignment; response-only training; stable crossentropy
exercises.why: A model can train without crashing while learning from the wrong token or padding. This exercise makes target alignment and the actual training objective explicit.
exercises.brief: Implement next_token_loss(logits,tokens,loss_mask,pad_id), returning {'loss': mean_loss, 'token_count': count, 'per_position': list}. tokens contains T token IDs and logits contains T rows of vocabulary-size V scores. Row t predicts tokens[t+1], NOT tokens[t]. loss_mask has T booleans; loss_mask[j] states whether target token j should contribute. Score positions t=0..T-2 only when loss_mask[t+1] is true AND tokens[t+1]!=pad_id. per_position has T-1 entries: None for excluded targets and stable crossentropy for included targets. Ignore the final logits row, which has no next-token target. Empty or length-one sequences return loss=0.0, token_count=0 and an empty per_position list. If every target is masked, return loss=0.0, token_count=0 with all None entries. Assume matching lengths, nonempty vocabulary when T>0, valid in-range token IDs and finite scores. Calculate crossentropy as logsumexp(row)-row[target], using max subtraction; never take log of an underflowed softmax. Prompt tokens usually have mask false and completion tokens true: importantly, the last prompt position predicts the first completion token. Do not mutate inputs. This objective is the bridge to teacher-forced transformer training and supervised fine-tuning.

import copy
import math
import random
import unittest
from solution import next_token_loss

class LanguageLossTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_empty_and_single(self):
        self.assertEqual(next_token_loss([],[],[],0),{'loss':0.,'token_count':0,'per_position':[]})
        self.assertEqual(next_token_loss([[0.,0.]],[1],[True],0),{'loss':0.,'token_count':0,'per_position':[]})
    def test_uniform_shift(self):
        r=next_token_loss([[0.,0.,0.]]*3,[1,2,1],[True]*3,0)
        self.assertEqual(r['token_count'],2);self.assertAlmostEqual(r['loss'],math.log(3))
    def test_target_alignment(self):
        r=next_token_loss([[0.,0.,8.],[0.,8.,0.],[100.,0.,0.]],[1,2,1],[True]*3,0)
        expected=math.log1p(2*math.exp(-8))
        self.assertEqual(r['token_count'],2);self.assertAlmostEqual(r['loss'],expected)
    def test_prompt_boundary_and_pad(self):
        logits=[[1.,2.,3.],[3.,2.,1.],[2.,3.,1.],[999.,0.,0.]]
        r=next_token_loss(logits,[1,2,1,0],[False,False,True,True],0)
        self.assertEqual(r['token_count'],1);self.assertIsNone(r['per_position'][0]);self.assertIsNone(r['per_position'][2])
        self.assertAlmostEqual(r['loss'],3+math.log(1+math.exp(-1)+math.exp(-2))-2)
    def test_no_eligible_tokens(self):
        r=next_token_loss([[0.,1.]]*3,[1,1,0],[False]*3,0)
        self.assertEqual(r,{'loss':0.,'token_count':0,'per_position':[None,None]})
    def test_extreme_logits(self):
        r=next_token_loss([[1000.,-1000.],[0.,0.]],[0,1],[False,True],0)
        self.assertTrue(math.isfinite(r['loss']));self.assertAlmostEqual(r['loss'],2000.)
    def test_shift_invariance_and_ignored_rows(self):
        rng=random.Random(51)
        for _ in range(10):
            logits=[[rng.uniform(-3,3) for _ in range(4)] for _ in range(5)];tokens=[1,2,3,1,2];mask=[False,False,True,True,False]
            before=copy.deepcopy(logits);a=next_token_loss(logits,tokens,mask,0)
            shifted=[[v+100 for v in row] for row in logits];b=next_token_loss(shifted,tokens,mask,0)
            self.assertAlmostEqual(a['loss'],b['loss']);self.assertEqual(logits,before)
            for j in (0,3,4):logits[j]=[999.,-999.,10.,-10.]
            self.assertEqual(next_token_loss(logits,tokens,mask,0),a)

if __name__=='__main__':unittest.main()
